rationale: Closing source item for the remaining budget: the shutdown contract, which is the last client-facing lifecycle promise not yet recorded. It is idempotent, marks the node Shutdown before returning, and its future is what actually waits for the background routines and closes the transport, while in-flight work is answered with shutdown or leadership-lost errors by the loops that own it.

investigations.question: What exactly does Shutdown promise to a caller - when is the node considered shut down, when do in-flight operations finish, and when is the transport released?
investigations.hypothesis: Shutdown is idempotent: the first call closes the shutdown channel, records the node as shut down, moves it to the Shutdown state and returns a future bound to the node, while later calls return a future with no node so nothing is closed twice. The returned future's Error() is what waits for the background routines and, when the transport implements WithClose, closes it; operations still queued for the FSM thread are answered with the shutdown error by the dispatching code rather than being left pending.
investigations.discriminator: Compare the fields set by the first and later Shutdown calls with what the returned future's Error does, and trace what happens to work that is mid-flight when the shutdown channel closes. A defect needs a call that reports completion before the routines stop, a second call that closes something twice, or in-flight clients left unanswered; idempotent return values plus a future that waits and closes, with explicit shutdown responses on the dispatch paths, refute the concern.
limitations: Source-only: no execution was requested in this turn; no shutdown was raced against in-flight operations.
The survey covers the processLogs dispatch path and the shutdown future; other paths that respond ErrRaftShutdown or ErrLeadershipLost were not enumerated exhaustively.
The behaviour of a transport that does not implement WithClose was not exercised; in that case only the routines are awaited.

knowledge.statement: Shutdown is idempotent and two-phased: the first call takes the shutdown lock, closes the shutdown channel, records the node as shut down, sets the Shutdown state and returns a shutdown future bound to the node, while subsequent calls return a bare shutdown future so nothing is closed twice. The bound future's Error waits for the node's goroutine group and then closes the transport if it implements WithClose; work that is queued for the FSM thread when the shutdown channel closes is answered with ErrRaftShutdown by the dispatching code instead of being left pending.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.Shutdown in the captured revision and to the dispatch paths that select on the shutdown channel, such as the processLogs batch handoff; the transport is only closed when it implements WithClose.

interpretations.rationale: The contract is coherent and the ordering is explicit. Shutdown takes a lock, and on the first call closes the shutdown channel, marks the node shut down, sets the Shutdown state and returns a future bound to the node; a later call returns a future whose raft pointer is nil precisely so that nothing is closed twice (api.go:1012-1025). Because the node is marked and moved to Shutdown before the future is returned, a caller that ignores the future still observes the state change, while a caller that waits obtains the stronger guarantee: the shutdown future's Error waits on the node's routine group and closes the transport when it implements WithClose (future.go:167-180), so the return value is the only thing that waits for background work rather than just requesting it. In-flight operations are not orphaned by the channel closing: the processLogs batch handoff selects on the shutdown channel and responds ErrRaftShutdown to every future in the batch it could not dispatch (raft.go:1300-1310), and the run loops return out of their select when the channel closes so their own pending futures are answered by the cleanup paths already recorded in this run (leadership-lost for the leader's inflight set). No defect is claimed: the two-phase shape, the idempotence and the explicit shutdown responses are consistent with each other, and the only boundary worth naming is that a caller who never waits on the future gets a request rather than a completed shutdown.
counterevidence: The second-call future carries a nil node deliberately, which is what prevents a double transport close rather than being an oversight.
The ordering (mark and change state under the lock, then return the future) means an ignored future cannot leave the node looking healthy.
limitations: Source-only; no shutdown was raced against in-flight operations in this run.
Only the processLogs handoff was cited as an in-flight response path; other shutdown response sites were not enumerated.
Transports without WithClose are awaited but not closed, which was read but not exercised.
